notes:
Topline: mid-market e-comm returns platform (merchant-facing) — building post-purchase support agents to reduce live CS load. Evaluating Redwood Hosted first for speed, then Dedicated for mainland scaling. Priority: tight p95 latency for chat/agent flows (customer expect near real-time responses), streaming + tool-calling for carrier lookups and label generation.

Key constraints: spikes 3x–5x during peak (BF/Cyber and holiday returns windows), multi-region routing (NA primary, EU residency required for some merchants), must preserve audit logs and KMS-managed keys. Cost sensitivity moderate: want to balance per-token spend vs. suppression of support headcount.

POC ask: 2-week hosted API POC (ingest sample transcripts + synthetic peak load). Success metrics: p95 end-to-end <= 600ms for agent utterance streaming (typical 2-3 turns), tool-calling latencies < 200ms (carrier lookup), fallbacks defined if latency/throughput degrade. Need transparent per-route cost breakdown.

Conversation highlights:
- Product lead (Maya Chen): "If we can guarantee sub-second responses during peak, we can justify moving to Dedicated."
- SE notes (Priya): demo showed streaming and tool-calling working but 95th latency spikes under synthetic peak — need kernel-level perf profile from Redwood.
- Security: legal asked for SOC2 evidence + KMS integration notes; EU merchants flagged data residency constraints.

Sales activities & asks: pricing band for Dedicated (4x GPUs) and burst capacity; optional on-prem packaging for high-risk enterprise merchants; SLA options and rollback/fallback policies.

Quote from merchant ops: "Returns are the top driver of contact volume — if agents can answer pre-emptively we save 40% of escalations."
